title: Два рыжих волоса и приглашение на ужин  (Two Red Hairs and a Dinner Invitation)

segments.t: Putting Sun Tzu's strategies into action, Max plucks two red hairs from Senya's head so he can pit the line cook against Ilya. Meanwhile, Chef Barinov calls Elena Pavlovna to smooth over the morning's awkwardness by inviting her to a formal dinner at Claude Monet.
Ты что делаешь?
Мне нужно два волоса.
А лучше два, вдруг один потеряю.
Зачем тебе мой волос?
Когда одиноко, смотреть на них и вспоминать.
Очень смешно.
Один готов.
Мне два волоса.
Кость, алло.
Сегодня вечером тебя ждет сюрприз.
Ведь, может, хватит сюрпризов на сегодня.
Ну, это и был мой сюрприз.
Давай, как будто я не знала.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
Ты что делаешь?
'What do you think you are doing?' Kostya brings out the contrast between 'you' and 'what' in a few short words. Max answers right away.
Мне нужно два волоса.
'I need two hairs from your head.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'for me' before landing on 'hair'.
А лучше два, вдруг один потеряю.
'Better make it two, just in case I lose one.' Here Kostya anchors the thought on 'better' and finishes on 'to lose', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
Зачем тебе мой волос?
'Why do you need my hair?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'what for' and finishing on 'hair'. Kostya answers right away.
Когда одиноко, смотреть на них и вспоминать.
'To look at them and remember you whenever I feel lonely.' Kostya brings out the contrast between 'when' and 'lonely' in a few short words.
Очень смешно.
'Very funny.' The meaning hinges on 'very' working together with 'funny' in spoken Russian.
Один готов.
'That is one down.' Notice how Russian expresses 'one' and 'ready' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Max answers right away.
Мне два волоса.
'I need two hairs.' Max anchors the line on 'for me', while 'hair' completes the thought.
Кость, алло.
'Kostya, hello.' In Russian, the idea of 'bones' flows naturally into 'hello' without extra filler words.
Сегодня вечером тебя ждет сюрприз.
'A surprise is waiting for you tonight.' Notice how Russian expresses 'today' and 'surprise' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Kostya answers right away.
Ведь, может, хватит сюрпризов на сегодня.
'Vitya, maybe we have had enough surprises for one day.' The grammar packs 'you know' and 'today' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Ну, это и был мой сюрприз.
'Well, that was supposed to be my surprise.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'come on' before landing on 'surprise'.
Давай, как будто я не знала.

'Go ahead, ask me as if I did not know.' The '-a' ending on the past-tense verb for 'knew' marks a female speaker or subject. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.

Ведь, может, хватит сюрпризов на сегодня.

That wraps up this scene as max plucks two red hairs from Senya's head for his scheme against Ilya, while Chef Barinov calls Elena Pavlovna to invite her to dinner at Claude Monet. See you next time!
